name: imscJS
role: Reference JS renderer drawing IMSC/TTML captions at any time offset into a DOM element
summary: imscJS (npm imsc 2.0.0) parses an IMSC/TTML document with fromXML, resolves it at any time offset with generateISD and draws it with renderHTML, so a browser scene can show captions exactly as an IMSC player lays them out (regions, styles, overlap) while seeking by frame time.
use_when: A burnt-in caption preview or delivery check that must follow IMSC/TTML region and style rules
Captions in a seek-driven browser scene captured to frames with alpha
Over libass when the source is TTML, not ASS or SRT
avoid_when: Checking line length, duration or overlap limits: caption-checker
Burning SRT or ASS into a video file: ffmpeg-ffprobe or libass
notes: 2026-11-27: Rendering needs a DOM (a browser, or a caller-supplied XML parser plus DOM in Node); final pixels depend on Chromium font fallback, so pin fonts for portable output. Roll-up keeps state between ISDs and was not tested. Version 2.0.0 migration notes were not checked.

assessment.rationale: npm imsc 2.0.0 published 2026-10-21 under BSD-2-Clause; repository pushed 2026-11-20. Neighbours ttconv (converts) and caption-checker (checks limits) draw nothing; this is the only catalogue route that renders IMSC styling and regions at an arbitrary offset, which suits seek-driven capture.

evidence.result: IMSC1 document (2 regions, italic, line break, overlap) seeked per frame in Chromium: 60 frames at 640x360 with alpha; getMediaTimeEvents [0,2,2.5,3,4,5]; 5 distinct frames; alpha max 1 at frames 5, 27, 35 and 0 at 22, 55; shuffled hashes equal sequential. Frames inspected.
evidence.scope: One IMSC1 text document, no roll-up, forced display or images, system sans-serif fallback, Playwright Chromium on macOS arm64; not other documents, fonts or browsers.
